title: LLM-adjacent competitor feature mapping and signal bucketization
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Create a repeatable playbook and first-pass artifact that maps near-term competitor offerings and adjacent open models into a capability-feature matrix, then bucket observed signals into structured categories that the Product and GTM teams can use for prioritization and alerts. This ticket delivers: 1) a Competitor Feature Map (CFM) covering latency/cost profiles, deployment modes, tooling hooks (function-calling, streaming, embeddings), and enterprise controls; 2) a Signal Taxonomy for ingestion (public releases, benchmark spikes, pricing changes, partner integrations, open-source forks); 3) a prioritization rubric to convert signals into action (scout, experiment, escalate); and 4) a first 30-day monitoring dashboard prototype.

Scope decisions and trade-offs: We will focus on north-star attributes relevant to Redwood Inference: serving economics (latency/cost on 8xA100-equivalent), deployment compatibility (hosted/dedicated/private), and operational integrations (KMS, SSO, audit logs). We intentionally deprioritize deep model-architectural analysis (e.g., transformer internals) for now to keep scope deliverable in 2 weeks. The trade-off is fewer low-level signals but faster iteration on product / GTM changes.

Deliverables: 
- Competitor Feature Map (spreadsheet + narrative): rows = vendor/model, columns = capability buckets (latency @256 tokens, token cost estimate, streaming support, embeddings parity, function-calling, quantization profiles available, private-deploy support, documented SLA, enterprise controls, partner marketplace presence). Link: https://drive.redwood.ai/pm/CFM-13021
- Signal Taxonomy doc (Confluence): buckets = Release, Performance Benchmark, Pricing/License, Partnership/Marketplace, Vulnerability/Compliance, Community Fork. Each bucket includes signal weight and initial alert thresholds.
- Prioritization Rubric (sheet): convert weighted signals + customer usage overlap into recommended action: Scout / Benchmark / Roadmap / Sales Alert.
- Dashboard prototype: Grafana panel + Notion alert flow for signals hitting thresholds (demo link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/pm-signals)

Stakeholders & Owners: Marco Chen (owner, PM), Aisha Patel (product lead), Priya Rao (research, ad-hoc model tests), Leon Ortiz (engineering liaison for benchmark runs), Sofia Marin (solutions / GTM). Eng support: ENG-2211 will provide costed benchmark runs and standardized test harness.

Success criteria (by due_date): CFM completed for top 12 competing vendors/models; Signal Taxonomy approved by PM + Research; Dashboard prototype ingests at least two live feeds (Hugging Face releases, pricing RSS) and surfaces alerts; Rubric converted into two playbook actions used by Growth and DevRel.

Risks & Mitigations: 
- Risk: Benchmarks inconsistent across vendors. Mitigation: Use normalized 8xA100-equivalent numbers and note testing conditions. ENG to standardize harness by EOD 2026-02-12.
- Risk: Noise-heavy signals create alert fatigue. Mitigation: Start with conservative thresholds and add manual triage pipeline (owner: Priya Rao).

Next steps (short term):
1) Marco to schedule kickoff with Research + Eng (done, meeting 2026-02-09). 
2) Leon to deliver baseline benchmark harness and run 3 sample models by 2026-02-11 (in progress). 
3) Priya to prototype taxonomy and seed 50 historical signals into the classification sheet by 2026-02-13 (in progress).
4) Draft CFM skeleton and circulate to GTM for feedback by 2026-02-16.

Longer-term: Integrate with Monitor/Alerting infra and wire up to Console rollouts as automated triggers for canary deployments when we detect aggressive competitor pricing or performance claims.
